description: Phase 9 certified the year-end annualization from payroll runs the engine calculated itself. A company that switches payroll provider part-way through the year brings the earlier months as imported history: source-of-truth totals that join the annualization without being recalculated. Phase 13 certifies that join with a real engine run for the months after the switch: the combined gross, contributions, withholding and 13th month, the 13th month already paid by the previous provider, the year boundary, and the fail-closed refusals. Every expected value is an immutable literal derived by hand from the BIR table and is never computed with PayrollPH functions.

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN, annual table effective 2023 onward: taxable income <= 250,000 exempt; to 400,000 at 15% over 250,000 (22,500 at 400,000); to 800,000 at 22,500 + 20% over 400,000 (102,500 at 800,000); to 2,000,000 at 102,500 + 25% over 800,000.
sources.thirteenthMonthAndBenefits: NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e) as amended by TRAIN: 13th-month pay and other benefits share one exemption of 90,000. PD 851 / DOLE: 13th-month pay is one twelfth of the basic salary actually earned in the calendar year, so the months earned under the previous provider count toward the entitlement, and what that provider already paid is not paid twice.
sources.substitutedFiling: BIR RR 2-98 as amended: the employer that files the year's certificate annualizes the whole year's compensation, so compensation and tax withheld by a previous payroll provider of the same employer belong in the one annualization.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs. The company switched provider on 2026-07-01: January to June are imported monthly rows (pay date = last day of the month), July to December (cutoffs 13-24) are calculated by the engine, 'split' statutory timing.

Each worker earns PHP 30,000 a month, so a calculated cutoff is exactly the Phase 9 steady cutoff: gross 15,000, SSS 750, PhilHealth 375, Pag-IBIG 100, withholding 503.70. An imported month carries twice that: gross and basic 30,000, SSS 1,500, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 200, withholding 1,007.40, net 26,542.60, unless a case says otherwise.

Imported rows are inserted exactly as the migration importer stores them (source system, unique source reference per worker, basic salary earned, contributions, tax, 13th month). The importer itself is covered by its own tests.
Regular payroll runs do not pay 13th month, so the engine-calculated months pay none; the entitlement is the accrued basic of the whole year divided by 12, less what the previous provider paid.
Year-end annualization reads Released runs, so each calculated run is set to Released directly in the fixture.

sameFiguresAsOneEmployer.description: Six imported months identical to calculated ones. The year is the Phase 9 steady worker: gross 360,000 + accrued 13th month 30,000 = 390,000; contributions 6 x 2,450 + 12 x 1,225 = 29,400; non-taxable 30,000 + 29,400 = 59,400; taxable 330,600; tax 15% over 250,000 = 12,090.00 + 0 = 12,090.00. Withheld 6 x 1,007.40 + 12 x 503.70 = 12,088.80: collect 1.20.

previousProviderOverWithheld.description: The previous provider withheld 1,200.00 a month instead of 1,007.40 (7,200.00 in six months). Tax due is unchanged at 12,090.00; withheld 7,200.00 + 6,044.40 = 13,244.40; refund 12,090.00 - 13,244.40 = -1,154.40.

thirteenthPaidByPreviousProvider.description: The previous provider paid the full 30,000 13th month in its June row (gross 60,000 that month, no extra contribution or tax because the amount is exempt). The year's 13th month is max(entitlement 30,000, paid 30,000) = 30,000 and nothing is accrued again: gross 5 x 30,000 + 60,000 + 12 x 15,000 = 390,000, the same year as the steady worker (taxable 330,600, tax 12,090.00, withheld 12,088.80): collect 1.20, with the 13th month counted once.

deMinimisWithinCeilings.description: The previous provider paid a rice subsidy of 2,500 in each of the six months (the monthly ceiling), inside gross pay of 32,500 a month (basic 30,000). Imported de minimis is exempt up to its ceiling: 6 x 2,500 = 15,000 exempt, nothing above the ceiling. Gross 6 x 32,500 + 12 x 15,000 + accrued 13th month 30,000 = 405,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 15,000 + 29,400 = 74,400; taxable 330,600; tax 12,090.00; withheld 12,088.80: collect 1.20, the same as the steady worker because the subsidy is not taxed.

deMinimisAboveMonthlyCeiling.description: Rice subsidy of 3,000 a month (ceiling 2,500), gross 33,000 a month. Per month 2,500 is exempt and 500 is the excess: 15,000 exempt, 3,000 excess. The excess joins the shared 90,000 pool with the 13th month (30,000 + 3,000 = 33,000, under the cap, so it is still not taxed). Gross 6 x 33,000 + 180,000 + 30,000 = 408,000; non-taxable pool 33,000 + 15,000 + 29,400 = 77,400; taxable 330,600; tax 12,090.00; withheld 12,088.80: collect 1.20.

deMinimisAnnualCeilingAcrossMonths.description: Uniform allowance of 2,000 in each of the six months against the 8,000 ANNUAL ceiling: 12,000 paid, so 8,000 is exempt and 4,000 is the excess, however the months fall. Gross 6 x 32,000 + 180,000 + 30,000 = 402,000; the pool is 30,000 + 4,000 = 34,000; non-taxable 34,000 + 8,000 + 29,400 = 71,400; taxable 330,600; tax 12,090.00; withheld 12,088.80: collect 1.20.

rowsOutsideTheTaxYearAreIgnored.description: The same six months plus two imported rows outside the year: pay date 2025-12-31 (gross 999,999.99, tax 99,999.00, 13th month 5,000) and 2027-01-01 (gross 888,888.88, tax 88,888.00). Neither belongs to 2026, so the year is exactly the first case: collect 1.20.

controls.description: Run in a separate fictional employer whose worker has ONE released cutoff (cutoff 13). A refused settlement must leave no adjustment rows. After the refusals the bad imported rows are removed and the worker is settled on one calculated cutoff: gross 15,000 + accrued 13th month 15,000/12 = 1,250 = 16,250; non-taxable 1,250 + 1,225 = 2,475; taxable 13,775; tax 0.00; withheld 503.70; refund 503.70.
controls.deMinimisLeaveDaysRefusal: cannot be applied to imported totals

limitations: Imported rows are inserted as the importer stores them; the importer's parsing, mapping and approval are covered by its own tests, not here.

Imported de minimis is capped per statutory category and period (month, semester, year by pay date) at the RR 29-2025 ceilings in force; the part inside the ceiling is exempt and the excess joins the shared 90,000 pool. Monetized leave days and the daily overtime meal allowance cannot be proven from imported totals and are refused. Imported de minimis is not combined with de minimis grants calculated by the engine for the same worker (the payroll run already flags that combination for review).
Monthly imported rows only; semi-monthly imported rows aggregate the same way but are not separately exercised. Minimum wage earners with imported history are refused (certified), not supported.
The release approval workflow and the HTTP, role and MFA gates of the migration routes are not exercised.

The expected values follow the cited BIR rules and the repository's year-end treatment. They have not been reviewed by a qualified Philippine tax practitioner and must be before anyone relies on them for filing.
